data.name: Among the Sleep - Enhanced Edition
data.detailed_description:
Enhanced Edition

Among the Sleep é um premiado jogo de aventura de terror na primeira pessoa, onde assumes o papel de uma criança pequena que procura a sua mãe, depois de ser acordada por sons ameaçadores a meio da noite. 

A versão melhorada de Among the Sleep contém gráficos aprimorados, um livro de arte digital e banda sonora integrada no jogo, pijamas selecionáveis, puzzles e jogabilidade melhorados, novos diálogos e um novíssimo nível de museu, onde podes explorar os bastidores e experimentar cenas e conceitos que foram cortados do jogo e nunca foram vistos.


Acerca do jogo

Um jogo de terror na primeira pessoa onde controlas uma criança de dois anos.

O jogo explora o horror por meio da atmosfera e exploração, mas não com música e sistemas de combate. Em Among the Sleep você está vulnerável, assustado, tentando entender o mundo ao seu redor.

O jogo conta com suporte ao Oculus Rift DK1, mas não trará suporte para outros tipos. Este jogo não estará disponível para HTC Vive.

O que as pessoas estão dizendo

  • "Bis!" - Kotaku

  • "[...] ele excede as expectativas na criação de uma atmosfera incrivelmente sinistra, com ansiedade pueril, e lida com um tema sério de forma comovente e sombria."- IGN

  • "A representação de uma história de horror em primeira pessoa pelos olhos e perninhas cambaleantes de uma criança de dois anos é o mais intrigante que já vimos neste ano inteiro, remontando àquela época em que os jogos buscavam novas maneiras de jogar e novas histórias para contar."- Eurogamer

[/list]

reviews.review:
I quite like Among The Sleep. I watched some of my favourite YouTubers play when I was younger and enjoyed watching the game. I did find some of its darker elements, somewhat alarming but it was also easier to get into the character’s mindset being young myself at the time. Whereas nowadays I felt more protective of the toddler character.

I would [b]recommend[/b] the game. [i]However[/i], I will add that the game focuses on [b]themes of 
 neglect and addiction[/b], and anyone who struggles with these themes should be wary of them. I think it represents what it is trying to go for quite well.

I found its game design to be very well done, being small in scale (literally in character and being a rather small game) and actually being able to make the player resonate with the sense of scale and with animations (for example, falling over because the toddler hasn't learned how to properly walk (although I will note, this did not occur frequently enough to become annoying, in fact falling added to the stress of some of the chase sequences by having you fall at crucial times leading to immense panic as you try to stand back up.)). It was fascinating to theorise who or what the monsters (the witch woman, or the coat wearing bright eyed, shadow creature) lurking in the darkness was. The game uses the player's imagination to wonder what the monster is, unlike the child who just seems desperate to navigate around it and try to understandably escape it.

The controls were fine, they were kept immersive. Climbing up some things could be a little wonky at times and I did wish the climbing animation was a little faster, but it is understandable as it added to the tension and this didn’t hinder my experience, despite my understanding that the hitbox was further away and I didn’t need to worry that much. Although, one mission I struggled in was escaping from the witch in the forest, it was unclear where to go and even when I did find out where to go I needed a green key. The game isn’t particularly difficult but this one section had me stumped on where to go or what to do more than any of the other excellently designed levels.

I found some of the drawings to be in hard to locate places and ended up needing a [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=627895487]guide[/url]. Other than having to restart a chapter when I missed one they were fairly easy to collect.

I liked the game's sound choice and how the environment was handled because it remained in a actual dream/nightmare parts and continued to keep the player in a heightened state (like hiding and running away from the monsters) to be immersed with the toddler's sense of fear.

I thought the VA of the mother (Cia Court) played the role well between initially what seems a sweet and doting mother and [spoiler]a struggling alcoholic who may have a tendency to neglect her child. The “why are you always hiding from mommy” line was particularly sinister on replay.[/spoiler]

[h1]Story Spoilers[/h1]

[spoiler]The difference and truth sadly, is that the child [i]technically[/i] knows [i]who[/i] the creature is, he just cannot understand [i]why[/i] they behave that way and therefore perceives the creature as two separate entities (his sober kind mother, and the intoxicated demonic shrieking monster she becomes when under the influence of alcohol), given the toddler clearly sees the world in black and white. An example; his mother in the intro, face brightly smiling, but contrasted by the enshrouding darkness following them as she carries him to bed. The truth of the monster is revealed in ([i]if you didn't guess it[/i]) the ending; the prologue expands on this concept further with you free to explore the rest of the house.[/spoiler]

[spoiler]I felt the introduction was handled well and suspected (like a lot of the reactors I watched) that the father was [i]potentially[/i] the one who was abusive and kicked out by the mother, since it was the mother saying 'NO' to him and at the beginning we, much like the toddler, don't understand what is truly going on. Of course, this is to later subvert expectations with the ending of the game. Some of the drawings also hint toward the truth.[/spoiler]

[spoiler]The prologue I found interesting as it further explains that the father may not have been as innocent as the mother seemed at first either, neither in the right. However, the game does its best to frame the mother as this terrifying monster, and it is the only side we truly see, being that of an alcoholic neglectful struggling single mother who seems to truly hate her child for whatever reason. One of the most memorable lines the mother had for me personally was “it’s too much” (the responsibility of her own child is too much.) which she also restates in the prologue, assuming the child is not being affected or not caring, and being obviously neglectful like leaving the window open for the toddler during what seemed (although could of been exaggerated from the child’s perspective like their stuffed toys come to life) like a blizzard.[/spoiler]

[h2]The Ending[/h2]

[spoiler]I sympathised with the child, and despite previously feeling sympathetic for the mother. This time, I completely disliked her. In fact, all I felt when she pushes the toddler away is a 'want to protect' since all he wanted was his teddy bear and quite frankly clearly doesn't have time for her bs.[/spoiler]

[spoiler]I forgot if you reapproach the mother the toddler pats her head, I did not like this gesture and chose to reload my save purely to walk straight past her after the push, and leaving her to cry in her own misery, after being obviously neglectful; like (in the prologue) not caring, and instead leaving the window open for the toddler to freeze (potentially to death, while she drinks and feels sorry for herself) and potentially trying to kill him by throwing him out of a crib onto the floor, during chapter 2.[/spoiler]

[spoiler]In my opinion in terms of truth of the story, the game leaves it ambiguous, you know the parents fought. My problem is regardless of what we learn about the father, the mother has done nothing since the introduction cutscene except try to kill us, hunt us down and chase us (regardless of whether in the child’s dreams (like if he fell asleep in the closet hiding from his mother who was trashing his room) in a fit of drunk hysteria).[/spoiler]

[spoiler]It left me wanting more, to understand the father more but primarily it left me wondering whether the toddler would truly be safe or whether this evil he knew was actually better. Regardless, the game paints the mother out to be the worser of the two evils, from neglect if not downright abuse. Nowadays, I just wanted the abusive b**** of a mother to fuck off, but unfortunately, was left unsure of what that would mean for him with his father.[/spoiler]
